title: Lesson 44 - Designing a Segment for a Business Goal: Audience, Criteria, and Testing Before Publish
description: Define basic concepts of segmentation and use cases, focused on turning a business goal into a designed segment by choosing the audience, selecting criteria, and testing before it ships.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the recommended way to design a new segment?
options: Open the data model object with the most fields and filter until the count looks reasonable
State the business goal as audience, condition, and action, then map each part to an object, criteria, and a destination
Build the largest possible audience and let the campaign team narrow it
Base the segment only on data lake objects
questions.explanation: Design begins with the goal expressed as audience, condition, and action, then maps to an object, criteria, and a destination; data-first design and unordered audiences produce unused or wrong segments.

questions.question: A consultant must build an audience of people whose criteria rely on recent order behavior. What is the best approach?
options: Segment on Sales Order so each order becomes a member
Segment on Unified Individual and reach order attributes through relationships
Segment on a data lake object holding the raw orders
Segment on the Segment Membership object
questions.explanation: To reach people, build on Unified Individual and traverse to order data through relationships; segmenting on Sales Order yields orders, and data lake objects are not segmentable targets.

questions.question: A segment preview returns fewer members than expected. Which cause is most likely?
options: The lookback window or a container whose criteria override it narrowed the data range
The segment type was standard instead of dynamic
The data space is not the default space
questions.explanation: A narrow lookback window or a container that overrides it shrinks the data range and drops members; preview is available to users with the right segment and data permissions.
